findings.title: Two documented target-parser behaviours are unreachable by any test: the direct `db.<ref>.` form and the unparseable-target refusal
findings.reason: NOT FIXED -- WIDENED by the fix. The fix deleted mint-admin's own `refFromDatabaseTarget` and made `assertMintTarget` take `dbProjectRef` from the caller, produced by `extractProjectRefForLog` (`scripts/staging-guard.ts:154-165`). At round-1 HEAD the pooler branch WAS covered (round 1 recorded only `:208` direct and `:194` invalid-URL as 0-covered); at round-2 HEAD none of it is. findings.title: Fragile assertion: the new TARGET-line test cannot see the TARGET line lose its project ref
findings.reason: `it('leads every report with the TARGET line')` asserts `expect(line).toContain(STAGING_REF)` where `line = formatMintTarget(target)`, then `expect(formatMintReport(...)[0]).toBe(line)`. The second assertion compares the function's output to itself -- it is a tautology over content -- and the first cannot discriminate, because ALL THREE fixture fields contain `STAGING_REF` (`projectRef` is the ref, `supabaseHost` is `<ref>.supabase.co`, `databaseTarget` is `postgres.<ref>@...`). Mutation M9 deleted `project=${target.projectRef} ` from `formatMintTarget` and SURVIVED. Review finding S1 exists precisely so the operator sees which project they are pointed at before the first write; nothing pins that field. Fix: assert the whole line against an expected string built from three DISTINCT fixture values, e.g. `expect(line).toBe(`TARGET: project=${STAGING_REF} supabase=${host} db=${dbTarget}`)` with a `projectRef` that does not appear in the other two.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The mutant changes the emitted string, so it is not equivalent in general. Against the behaviour this test NAMES -- that the report leads with the TARGET line -- the mutant preserves it, so the survivor is recorded `inconclusive`/`oracle` rather than a confirmed P0. The defect is in the oracle, and that is the finding.

findings.title: The new `['database project ref', dbProjectRef]` prod-denylist row has no oracle
findings.reason: Mutation M4 deleted the row from `assertMintTarget`'s production-denylist loop and SURVIVED. The only test that reaches the prod branch (`refuses a production project ref outright`) also passes a prod `supabaseUrl`, which throws first. P2 rather than P1 because for the sole production caller the row is redundant: `main()` derives `dbProjectRef` by substring extraction from `config.databasePoolUrl`'s hostname or username, and `dbTarget` = `${username}@${hostname}:${port}` is a superset of both, so any prod ref in `dbProjectRef` is already in `dbTarget` -- which IS checked. It is not PROVABLY equivalent, because `assertMintTarget` is exported and a future caller could pass an unrelated pair. Fix: one case passing a clean supabaseUrl/dbTarget with a prod `dbProjectRef`.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Executed but indistinguishable under the current fixture; recorded inconclusive/oracle.

findings.arbiter_reasoning: The mutant changes `isDuplicateEmailError` for inputs outside this fixture, so it is not equivalent in general; against THIS input the function's result is unchanged, so it is recorded `inconclusive`/`oracle` rather than a confirmed P0. The gap is in the fixture, not in production behaviour.
